narrative: Regime read: Cautiously Neutral (composite score -0.02 on a -1 to +1 scale, 36th percentile of all trading days since 1999). Finance conditions are roughly balanced (-0.06), economic data is supportive (+0.17), and market psychology leans fearful (-0.20), with the economy in an Expansion phase.

Finance: the yield curve is positively sloped (+0.38pp), the S&P 500 trades at 25.1x earnings against a ~16.5x historical average, and 3 of 5 tracked sectors are positive over the past month — the classical efficient-market / factor-based baseline this dashboard's behavioral overlay adjusts. Economics: ISM PMI is at 55.5 (expansion), CPI is running 3.7% YoY against a 3.88% Fed funds rate, and unemployment sits at 4.1%. ISM PMI at 55.5 shows expansion, with neither the yield curve nor unemployment flashing late-cycle strain. (standard business-cycle framing — sentiment reads differently depending on where the cycle stands.)

Fundamentals (finance + economics) alone would put the read at +0.04; current psychology shifts that to -0.02 — a 0.06-point gap that makes positioning more cautious than fundamentals alone would justify. Psychology is weighted 23% of the final read right now (up from a 15% calm-market floor) because of how extreme it currently is. Per the Adaptive Markets Hypothesis this dashboard is built on, that gap — not any single pillar — is the actual signal.

No single extreme-positioning signal (herding, loss-aversion-driven hedging, overconfidence, or a Minsky-style extended-calm streak) is flashing right now — sentiment, hedging demand, and volatility all look within a normal range.
